subject: Secure ingress handoff — direct routing vs managed endpoint vs encrypted tunnel
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finport.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11 09:12 PDT
Subject: Secure ingress handoff: options for Redwood Private at FinPort

Jonas / Camila —

Thanks for the RFC call last week. Attached is our simplified network diagram and a short list of constraints for the pilot (network-diagram-v2.pdf). High level:
- Low latency requirement for inference calls (p95 < 60ms from our app tier in us-west-2)
- Strong audit trail (flow logs + preserved source IPs where possible)
- No transitive routing through third-party VPCs (FinPort policy)
- Cross-account: Redwood will own the inference VPCs; FinPort will control app VPCs
- Multi-AZ, single-region to start; potential multi-region later

Can you outline pros/cons for the three handoff approaches we discussed: direct routing (VPC peering / cross-account route tables), managed endpoint (PrivateLink-style interface endpoint), and an encrypted site-to-site IPsec tunnel behind a NAT? We'd also appreciate any quick checklist of operational steps for each option and an initial recommendation for a 30-day pilot.

Attach: network-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Network Engineer — FinPort
netops@finport.com

(Attachment: network-diagram-v2.pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finport.com>, NetOps Team <netops@finport.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11 13:04 PDT
Subject: Re: Secure ingress handoff: options for Redwood Private at FinPort

Alice — thanks for the clear constraints and the diagram. I pulled together a concise comparison and an action checklist (attached: comparison-matrix.xlsx, latency-trace-20250510.pcap).TL;DR recommendation: start with PrivateLink-backed NLB in us-west-2 for the pilot, with a site-to-site IPsec tunnel as a cold standby for failover testing. Rationale below.

Option A — Direct routing (cross-account VPC peering / route tables)- Pros: native L3 routing, minimal per-GB charges inside same AZ/region in many clouds, source IP preserved end-to-end, low latency (no additional proxies).
- Cons: not supported across accounts as a managed endpoint (so requires explicit route exchange and strict IGW/NAT/route table hygiene). Transitive peering risk (must actively prevent). Harder to enforce service boundary and IAM-based access control. Cross-region requires additional peering or transit gateway.
- Operational notes: configure explicit owner-only route tables, add strict security-group rules, enable VPC Flow Logs to a FinPort-owned S3/Logging account for audit. Test for asymmetric routing and MTU issues (PMTU).

Option B — Managed interface endpoint (PrivateLink-style)- Pros: strong service isolation (Redwood exposes an interface endpoint / ENI; FinPort consumes it). Egress flow stays inside provider fabric; no peering relationships, avoids transitive routing. Fine-grained IAM/service policies and easier to swap backend model instances behind NLB.
- Cons: per-GB and per-hour endpoint charges; potential hairpinning if FinPort needs to call back into their own resources; source IP preservation typically requires proxying (X-Forwarded-For) or surrogate IPs — need to plan for TLS mutual auth if source identity is required. Usually region-scoped (cross-region adds complexity).
- Operational notes: deploy NLB in Redwood VPC, front with PrivateLink (interface endpoint) that creates ENIs in FinPort subnets. Ensure health checks use host-based checks to avoid blackhole on stale ENIs. Validate limits for ENIs and ephemeral port exhaustion.

Option C — Site-to-site IPsec tunnel to a NAT/proxy- Pros: simple from FinPort perspective (standard VPN), supports multi-vendor and multi-cloud, source IP can be NATed or preserved depending on design. Good fallback option for DR.
- Cons: adds hop and NAT/translation overhead, higher latency and jitter, and NAT hides client IPs unless we build an X-Forwarded-For chain. Operational complexity for scaling (multiple tunnels per AZ), and monitoring is heavier (BGP/SA lifetime).

Pilot recommendation and checklist (30-day):
1) Pilot topology: PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2 to avoid transitive peering and give strong isolation. Backend: Redwood NLB -> inference fleet behind autoscaling.
2) Configure mutual TLS at the app layer for end-to-end identity; use Private CA certs (Redwood can supply or integrate with FinPort’s KMS).
3) Enable VPC Flow Logs and mirror to FinPort logging bucket with lifecycle policy.
4) Run latency baseline (attached pcap) and run canary subset of traffic (1–5% initially).
5) Implement a cold standby S2S VPN (IPsec) configuration for failover testing; document failover playbook.
6) Define SLOs, tracing hooks, and a cost cap for the pilot (Kim can help with cost numbers).

Open questions for FinPort: expected sustained RPS, TLS termination preferences (Redwood edge vs FinPort), whether FinPort requires preserved client IP for fraud/eval reasons, and any strict MTU or DLP limitations.

Next step: 60-minute deep dive early next week to agree on pilot topology and collect credentials for a temporary endpoint. Proposed times: Tue 2025-05-13 10:00 or Wed 2025-05-14 09:00 PT.

Attachments: comparison-matrix.xlsx, latency-trace-20250510.pcap

— Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-05-12 08:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Secure ingress handoff: options for Redwood Private at FinPort

Adding a couple of operational cost notes to Jonas's excellent write-up:
- PrivateLink typically has an hourly endpoint fee + per-GB processing costs. For heavy inference workloads this can dominate. Recommend we run a quick cost model (I sketched one in the spreadsheet under the "cost assumptions" tab).
- VPC peering may look cheaper but cross-AZ/region transfer costs and NAT egress on FinPort side can erode savings.
- VPN is cheap to start but remember managed VPNs can cost more once you scale multiple tunnels/AZs.

If FinPort is price-sensitive we should quantify the per-100M token delta (I can convert bytes -> tokens if they share expected payload sizes). Also: confirm whether FinPort requires traffic to egress through a FinPort-owned NAT for outbound IP allowlisting — that affects architecture choice.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: comparison-matrix.xlsx - cost assumptions tab highlighted)

Team —
Short commercial note: FinPort has indicated a pilot window of ~30 days during discovery. Can we treat this as a paid pilot? I propose a small committed pilot (deal id FIN-2025-078) to cover reserved capacity + engineering time. Legal will need a DPA and a short SOW that calls out the pilot objectives, traffic cap, and rollback plan.

If we lean PrivateLink for the pilot I'm happy to pull in procurement and legal to speed contracting.

Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finport.com>

Date: 2025-05-13 15:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Secure ingress handoff: options for Redwood Private at FinPort

Thanks, all — helpful. A few clarifications and decisions from FinPort side:
- Transitive routing is a hard no. That alone pushes us toward an interface endpoint model for the pilot (PrivateLink).
- We need preserved client IP for fraud scoring; if PrivateLink removes source IP the backend must accept X-Forwarded-For and have robust mutual TLS to prove origin.
- Multi-region is not a blocker for later; start single-region (us-west-2) is fine.
- We'll approve a paid 30-day pilot under FIN-2025-078; procurement will send a PO once we see a short SOW.
- We'll schedule the deep dive Tue 2025-05-13 10:00 PT — that time works for our team (I'll send a calendar invite).

Action items I see:
1) Redwood: send a short SOW and pilot diagram for PrivateLink-backed NLB.
2) Redwood: confirm whether you can inject preserved client IP via X-Forwarded-For + mTLS.
3) FinPort: we will share expected payload sizes and steady-state RPS for the canary (expected peak ~150 RPS, payloads ~2.5 KB).
4) Legal/Procurement: exchange PO and DPA (Ben / Kimberly to coordinate).

Alice Zhang
Network Engineer — FinPort
netops@finport.com
